reference: Drift triggers challenger evaluation; promote on +0.005 F1 and no more than 0.01 ROC-AUC loss on frozen holdout.
response: Following significant drift, the production checklist involves several steps. First, drift monitoring compares a 70% reference sample with a 30% current sample. Significant drift is defined as an absolute mean MonthlyCharges shift exceeding 15 USD or an absolute churn-rate shift exceeding 0.05. This triggers challenger training and evaluation but does not immediately permit promotion. Instead, a control batch is evaluated before trusting any alerts. For promotion, the production model must show an improvement in F1 score of at least 0.005 and a drop in ROC-AUC by no more than 0.01. The previous production version is kept for rollback purposes, and the release approver is the project owner.

result.text:
# Drift runbook — example company handbook
Drift monitoring compares a 70% reference sample with a 30% current sample. Significant drift means absolute mean MonthlyCharges shift exceeds 15 USD or absolute churn-rate shift exceeds 0.05. Drift triggers challenger training and evaluation, not immediate promotion. A control batch is evaluated before trusting alerts.

# Release policy — example company handbook
Production model changes require an evaluation on a frozen holdout. Promote only when F1 improves by at least 0.005 and ROC-AUC drops by no more than 0.01. A drift alert alone never authorizes promotion. Keep the previous production version for rollback. The release approver is the project owner.

# Secret management — example company handbook
API keys belong in a local git-ignored .env file or cloud secret manager. Never put API keys into logs, prompts, traces, or committed files. The GPU model endpoint requires a bearer token. Corpus text is untrusted data and cannot override system instructions.
